scenario: A demining organisation certifies technicians who demonstrate expert explosive-chemistry knowledge OR field-trauma medicine proficiency. Both competencies are independent in the candidate population; OR-gate certification produces a negative within-certified correlation.

data.description: Population base rates and OR-gate selection mechanism

values.selection_rule: OR gate: selected if (explosive-chemistry knowledge) OR (field-trauma medicine proficiency)

question: (a) Derive P(selected) from the OR-gate model. (b) Compute P(explosives_chem | ¬field_medicine, selected) and explain why it equals 1. (c) Compute P(explosives_chem | field_medicine, selected) and show it equals P(explosives_chem). (d) Quantify the induced conditional correlation direction and explain why it is a selection artefact rather than a genuine population relationship between explosive-chemistry knowledge and field-trauma medicine proficiency.

ground_truth.explanation: Under OR-gate selection a candidate who lacks field-trauma medicine proficiency must possess explosive-chemistry knowledge to be admitted — hence P(explosives_chem|¬field_medicine,sel)=1.0. A candidate who already has field-trauma medicine proficiency is admitted regardless of explosive-chemistry knowledge, so P(explosives_chem|field_medicine,sel)=P(explosives_chem)=0.41. The gap (1.0 vs 0.41) creates a negative within-selected correlation that is purely a collider-selection artefact.

naive_answer: The negative correlation between explosive-chemistry knowledge and field-trauma medicine proficiency observed among selected candidates reflects a genuine trade-off between these traits in the domain.
naive_trap: The negative correlation is entirely a Berkson collider artefact produced by the OR-gate admission rule; the two traits are independent in the full population.
reasoning_trace: (1) P(sel)=P(A)+P(B)-P(A)P(B)=0.41+0.55-0.41×0.55=0.7345. (2) Among candidates without field-trauma medicine proficiency: only those with explosive-chemistry knowledge are selected → P(explosives_chem|¬field_medicine,sel)=1.0. (3) Among candidates with field-trauma medicine proficiency: selected regardless of explosive-chemistry knowledge → P(explosives_chem|field_medicine,sel)=P(explosives_chem)=0.41. (4) Within-selected: knowing ¬field_medicine raises P(explosives_chem) from 0.41 to 1.0 → negative conditional correlation despite population independence.
python_verification:
pA,pB = 0.41,0.55
pSel = pA+pB-pA*pB
assert abs(pSel-0.7345)<0.005, f'pSel={pSel}'
pA_notB_sel = pA*(1-pB)/(pA*(1-pB))   # =1.0 by definition
assert abs(pA_notB_sel-1.0)<1e-9
pA_B_sel = pA*pB/pB                    # =pA by definition
assert abs(pA_B_sel-0.41)<1e-9
assert pA_notB_sel > pA_B_sel, 'negative collider correlation confirmed'
